1. He showed me men sitting on a bench, and another man sitting on a chair. And he says to me, “Do you see the ones sitting on the bench?” “I see, sir,” I say. “These,” he says, “are faithful; and the one sitting on the chair is a false prophet who destroys the understanding of the servants of God—of the double‑minded, not of the faithful.[a]

2. These, then, the double‑minded, come to him as to a magician and ask him what will happen to them; and that false prophet, having in himself no power of a divine spirit, speaks with them according to their questions [and according to the desires of their wickedness], and fills their souls as they desire.[c]

3. For he, being empty, answers empty men with empty things; for whatever he is asked, he answers according to the emptiness of the person. But he also speaks some true words; for the devil fills him with his own spirit, if perhaps he may be able to tear away some of the righteous.

4. Therefore, as many as are strong in the faith of the Lord, having put on the truth, do not cling to such spirits, but keep away from them. But those who are double‑minded and often change their minds[b] practice divination like the nations and bring a greater sin upon themselves by practicing idolatry; for the one who consults a false prophet about any matter is an idolater, empty of the truth and foolish.

5. For no spirit given from God is consulted, but, having the power of the Deity, it speaks everything from itself, because it is from above, from the power of the divine Spirit.[d]

6. But the spirit that is consulted and speaks according to the desires of men is earthly and light, having no power; and it does not speak at all unless it is consulted.

7. “How then,” I say, “sir, will a person know which of them is a prophet and which is a false prophet?” “Listen,” he says, “about both prophets; and in the way I am about to tell you, so you shall test the prophet and the false prophet. Test the man who has the divine spirit by his life.

8. First of all, the one who has the [divine] spirit from above is gentle and quiet and humble‑minded, and refrains from every evil and from the vain desire of this age, and makes himself lower than all people; and when consulted he answers nothing to anyone, nor does he speak privately—nor does the holy Spirit speak whenever a person wishes it to speak—but it speaks when God wishes him to speak.

9. Therefore, when the man who has the divine spirit comes into a gathering of righteous men who have faith in the divine Spirit, and an intercession is made to God by the gathering of those men, then the angel of the prophetic spirit who is assigned to him fills the man; and being filled with the holy Spirit he speaks to the multitude as the Lord wills.[e]

10. Thus the spirit of the Deity will be made manifest. As for the spirit of the Deity of the Lord, this is its power.

11. “Hear now,” he says, “about the spirit that is earthly and empty and has no power, but is foolish.

12. First, that man who seems to have a spirit exalts himself and wants to have the first seat; and immediately he is presumptuous and shameless and talkative, and lives among many luxuries and many other deceits, and he receives payment for his prophecy; and if he does not receive it, he does not prophesy. Can a divine spirit receive payment and prophesy? A prophet of God cannot do this; rather, the spirit of such prophets is earthly.

13. Then, he does not come near a gathering of righteous men at all, but avoids them. He clings to the double‑minded and the empty, and he prophesies to them in a corner, and deceives them by speaking everything according to their desires, emptily; for he also answers the empty. For an empty vessel, placed together with empty ones, is not broken, but they agree with one another.

14. But when he comes into a gathering full of righteous men who have the spirit of divinity, and they offer intercession, that man is emptied. The earthly spirit flees from him out of fear, and the man becomes speechless and is completely shattered, unable to say anything.[f]

15. For if you pack a storeroom with wine or oil and place an empty jar among them, then later wish to unpack the storeroom, you will find the jar you placed there empty still. So too, when empty prophets come among the spirits of the righteous, they are found just as they came.

16. You have the way of life of both kinds of prophets. So test by his life and works the man who says that he bears a spirit.[g]

17. But you must trust the spirit that comes from God and has power. Put no trust in the earthly and empty spirit, because it has no power; it comes from the devil.

18. Listen, then, to the parable I am about to tell you. Take a stone and throw it toward heaven; see whether you can touch heaven. Or take a water tube and squirt water toward heaven; see whether you can pierce heaven.[h]

19. “How,” I say, “sir, can these things be? For you have said both these things are impossible.” “As these, then, are impossible, so also the spirits that are earthly are impossible and inert.

20. Take now the power that comes from above. Hail is a very small pellet, and when it falls on a man’s head, how much pain it causes! Or again, take a drop that falls from the roof tile to the ground, and it bores through the stone.

21. You see, then, that things from above, though very small when they fall upon the earth, have great power; so also the divine spirit that comes from above is powerful. Trust in this spirit, but keep away from the other.”

Paragraph 19: reconsideration of the prior rendering of ἀδύνατα; with spirits as its subject it means powerless, whereas with the feats it means impossible. He showed me men sitting on a bench and another man sitting on a chair. He asked, “Do you see the men on the bench?” “I see them, sir,” I said. “They are faithful,” he said. “The man on the chair is a false prophet. He destroys the understanding of God’s servants who waver, but not of those who are faithful.”[a]

2. People who waver go to him as they would to a magician. They ask what will happen to them. The false prophet has no power of a divine spirit in himself. He speaks according to their questions and their wicked desires. He fills their souls as they wish.[c]

3. He is empty, so he gives empty answers to empty people. Whatever they ask, he answers according to their emptiness. He does say some true words. The devil fills him with his own spirit, hoping to tear some of the righteous away.

4. Those who are strong in the Lord’s faith have put on the truth. They keep away from such spirits. But people who waver and often change their minds[b] practice divination like the nations. They commit idolatry and bring greater sin upon themselves. Anyone who consults a false prophet about any matter is an idolater, empty of truth and foolish.

5. No spirit given by God is consulted. It has the power of divinity and speaks everything from itself. It comes from above, from the divine spirit’s power.[d]

6. A spirit that answers questions according to people’s desires is earthly and light. It has no power. It does not speak at all unless someone consults it.

7. “Sir, how can a person tell a prophet from a false prophet?” I asked. He said, “Listen about both. What I am about to say will show you how to test them. Test the man who has the divine spirit by his life.”

8. “First, the man with the divine spirit from above is gentle, quiet and humble. He keeps away from every evil and this age’s empty desires. He makes himself lower than everyone. He gives no answer when consulted and does not speak privately. The holy Spirit does not speak whenever a person wants. It speaks when God wants the man to speak.”

9. “The man with the divine spirit comes into a gathering of righteous men who have faith in the divine Spirit. They offer intercession to God. Then the angel of the prophetic spirit assigned to him fills the man. Filled with the holy Spirit, he speaks to the gathering as the Lord wishes.”[e]

10. “This is how the spirit of divinity becomes clear. Such is the power of the Lord’s spirit of divinity.”

11. “Now listen about the earthly, empty spirit. It has no power and is foolish.”

12. “The man who seems to have a spirit exalts himself. He wants the first seat. He is immediately presumptuous, shameless and talkative. He lives in many luxuries and other deceits. He takes payment for his prophecy. If he is not paid, he does not prophesy. Can a divine spirit take payment and prophesy? A prophet of God cannot do this. Such prophets have an earthly spirit.”

13. “He avoids gatherings of righteous men. He stays close to people who waver and are empty. He prophesies to them in a corner. He deceives them with empty words that suit their desires. He gives empty people answers. An empty vessel placed with other empty vessels does not break. They agree with one another.”

14. “But he may enter a gathering full of righteous men who have the spirit of divinity. When they offer intercession, that man is emptied. The earthly spirit flees from him in fear. The man becomes speechless. He is completely shattered and cannot say anything.”[f]

15. “Suppose you pack a storeroom with wine or oil and put an empty jar among them. Later, when you unpack the room, you find that jar still empty. It is the same with empty prophets. When they come among the spirits of the righteous, they are found just as they came.”

16. “You have the way of life of both kinds of prophets. Test the man who says he bears a spirit by his life and works.”[g]

17. “Trust the spirit that comes from God and has power. Do not trust the earthly, empty spirit. It has no power and comes from the devil.”

18. “Listen to this parable. Take a stone and throw it toward heaven. See whether you can touch heaven. Or take a water tube and squirt water toward heaven. See whether you can pierce heaven.”[h]

19. “How can these things happen, sir?” I asked. “You have said both are impossible.” He said, “Just as these are impossible, earthly spirits are powerless and inactive.”

20. “Now consider the power that comes from above. A hailstone is a very small pellet. Yet how much pain it causes when it falls on a person’s head! Or consider a drop that falls from a roof tile to the ground. It bores through stone.”

21. “Very small things falling from above onto the earth have great power. In the same way, the divine spirit coming from above is powerful. Trust this spirit and keep away from the other.”

Athos, Lake Plate VIII, has “angel of the prophet.” Full alternative: “Then the angel of the prophet, assigned to him, fills the man; filled with the holy Spirit, the man speaks to the multitude as the Lord wills.” The draft provisionally retains the working phrase and records the shorter Greek alternative.
